To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plant controls on Late Quatenary ecosystem structure and function are greater than previously thought.
plant-soil interactions and the expansion of shrubs were key drivers of ecosystem change during the Late Quaternar extinction event in Britain.

1) the extinction of mega-herbive species had little effect on the structure and function of Late Quaternary terrestrial ecosystems in Britain and Ireland; 2) the expansion of woodyn plants and declining nitrogen availablity in the Late Quaternay were driven by warming temperatures, reduced burning and plant-plant and plant-soil interactions; 3) shrub biomass was one of the most powerful predictors of Late Quaternay ecosystem change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the structure and function of ecosystems has changed during the Late Quaternar
understanding how the structure and function of terrestrial ecosystems is controlled.
the role of plants in the functioning of ecosystems and the factors that control this.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

plant-soil and/or plant-plant interactions were the strongest controls on plant communities and nitrogen cycling during the Late Quaternar extinction event in Britain, and that the effects of mega-herbivor species were relatively weak.
plant species control ecosystem structure and function, but not necessarily to the same extent as animals, especially large herbivores.
plants and animals have an important role in the structure and function of ecosystems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plant controls on ecosystem structure and function are more important than previously thought, and that this is likely to be the case for other ecosystems as well.
plants are the primary drivers of terrestrial ecosystem structure and function.
plant-soil and biotic interactions are more important than mega-herbive control on terrestrial ecosystems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative importance of different factors controlling plant community structure and ecosystem function may change over time.
the relative importance of plants and animals in determining the fate of ecosystems may have been underestimated.
the effects of plant species on ecosystem functioning may be more important than the effects of herbivores.
